title: Investigating the Efficacy of a Professional Development Program in Formative Classroom Assessment in Middle School English Language Arts and Mathematics
extended_summary:
This paper evaluates whether a professional development program in formative classroom assessment improved middle school teachers’ assessment knowledge and their students’ achievement. The study was motivated by the claim that better classroom assessment practices should help teachers identify student learning needs and adjust instruction, but prior studies had produced mixed findings.

The intervention was a year-long professional development course developed by the South Carolina Department of Education. Teachers learned to align assessments to standards, write multiple-choice and performance items, build rubrics and checklists, interpret standardized tests, and use assessment results formatively and summatively. In Year 1, treatment schools received the program through trained assessment coaches while control schools received no professional development. In Years 2 and 3, the study compared the same professional development delivered by trained coaches versus relatively untrained facilitators, with matched comparison schools serving as controls.

The participants were sixth-, seventh-, and eighth-grade English language arts and mathematics teachers and their students in state-identified low-performing middle schools in South Carolina. Teacher knowledge was measured with pre/post assessment tests, and student achievement was measured using state PACT scores analyzed with multilevel models. The findings showed that the professional development improved teachers’ assessment knowledge in all years, regardless of whether it was delivered by a coach or facilitator. However, student achievement did not improve; in fact, treatment students often scored lower than comparison students, including significant negative effects in English language arts across all three years and in mathematics in Year 3. The authors conclude that improving teachers’ assessment skill alone may not be enough to raise achievement and that formative assessment must be linked to effective instructional action.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed multi-year study with a randomized cluster trial in Year 1 and quasi-experimental matched comparisons in Years 2-3, using multilevel modeling and standardized outcomes. However, only one year is fully randomized and later years rely on matched controls, so the design has some credibility concerns relative to a pure RCT.
impact_tier_rationale: The key student achievement effects are negative or null, with effect sizes mostly small and the largest magnitude around d=-0.33 in mathematics. Although teacher knowledge improved meaningfully, the paper reports no positive student achievement impact and in some cases a detrimental effect, which places overall impact in the red tier.

finding.finding_summary: This three-year study of middle school English language arts and mathematics teachers found that a formative assessment professional development program increased teacher assessment skill, but student achievement declined relative to matched controls. In English language arts, adjusted PACT scores were lower in the treatment schools by 2.39 points in Year 1 (d≈-0.16), 1.15 points in Year 2 (d≈-0.08), and 3.46 points in Year 3 (d≈-0.26); all three differences were statistically significant.
finding.measure: State standardized PACT English language arts scale scores

finding.finding_summary: In mathematics, there were no significant treatment effects in Years 1 and 2, but Year 3 showed significantly lower adjusted PACT scores for professional-development schools. The Year 3 adjusted difference was -3.76 points, with a standardized effect size of d≈-0.33; Years 1 and 2 were near zero (d≈0.03 and -0.01).
finding.measure: State standardized PACT mathematics scale scores

finding.finding_summary: The professional development produced clear gains in teachers’ assessment knowledge and related measurement skills, including aligning items to standards and identifying cognitive levels. On the teacher posttest, the treatment group improved by 8.51 points in Year 1 versus 1.85 points for controls, and both treatment conditions improved substantially in Years 2 and 3 (e.g., 10.99-11.77 points in Year 2; 8.00-8.23 points in Year 3), with significant pre-post effects (e.g., ω²=0.60 and 0.56).
finding.measure: Teacher assessment knowledge test / assessment skill pretest-posttest scores
finding.study_size: Year 1 n=151; Year 2 n=146; Year 3 n=71
